correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the exact spectral decomposition into dark weight-j projectors and d+1 simple, spectrally disjoint bright eigenvectors. PSD projector-compression identifies the full dark kernel by a finite but arbitrary-d Fourier induction. Odd closed-walk moments form a triangular nonsingular radial matrix, while dark odd contributions cancel by bipartite symmetry. Range intersection gives the marked rank and exact kernel; tensorized probabilities settle τ=0. Boundary d=1 and arbitrary real τ are explicitly covered. Exact symbolic dark checks for d<=5, moment checks for d<=4 and numerical mixing for d<=6 corroborate but do not replace proof. No proof step is based solely on finite experimentation.

value.rationale: A rank-one onsite defect on a Boolean cube is a natural quantum-search perturbation. The theorem precisely identifies an all-dimension rank jump of ceil(d/2) for any nonzero real defect and determines its surviving hidden Fourier sector. It gives a structural, physically interpretable all-start average transport invariant, not a numerical table or a trivial perturbation-bound corollary. Neither general projector formulas nor search success probabilities immediately yield the dark-kernel Fourier induction or radial moment certificate.
